The SDV paper is cited only as support for the claim that models trained on distorted synthetic data may fail on real customers, with no synthesizer run or method engaged.

To handle sparsity in participant-defined subgroups that made real-time fairness feedback impossible, the authors used SDV's Gaussian Copula Synthesizer to generate additional instances preserving realistic feature dependencies within the prototype's backend.

paper-enhancing-survival-analysis-federa.summary: This paper proposes FedSDS, a federated learning framework for survival analysis that uses a variational autoencoder-based synthetic data generator (SAVAE) to locally produce and share synthetic patient data across nodes, avoiding direct data sharing. It introduces a biased aggregation strategy aligned to local distributions, outperforming standard Federated Averaging under IID and non-IID, scarce-data healthcare scenarios. CTGAN is cited as related prior work in synthetic tabular data generation but is not the generator used in the proposed framework.

paper-estimating-longitudinal-impact-tra.summary: This paper builds a calibrated synthetic dataset of 2000 first-year engineering students across two semesters to compare traditional versus blended teaching methods, examining effort-efficiency trade-offs and drop/fail/withdraw outcomes over a full academic year. Baseline student attributes (prior preparation, SES proxy, self-efficacy) are synthesized to preserve realistic joint mixed categorical-continuous distributions before weekly dynamics are simulated on top. The synthetic-data generation step is attributed to a 'Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) approach', citing the CTGAN paper for its conditional sampling and mode-specific handling of mixed-type tabular data.

paper-hdlss-raman-gan-genetic-2026.summary: Works in the high-dimension low-sample-size regime of surface-enhanced resonance Raman spectroscopy, where a clinical serum study yields only 37 patients but each spectrum is long, and asks whether a genetic algorithm can tune a generator well enough to synthesise usable spectra for acute myocardial infarction detection. A basic genetic algorithm and NSGA-II search the hyperparameter space of three architectures, with a weighted sum of cosine similarity, likeness score, Wasserstein distance and Euclidean distance as the fitness function, and the search-optimised models beat manually tuned ones. CTGAN is one of the three architectures trained and searched, alongside WGAN-GP and CTAB-GAN+, and its own hyperparameters are the search space, with the paper referring readers to Xu et al. for their definitions. The paper reports CTGAN as the architecture that collapses at these sample sizes, being the most sensitive to the minimum sample number, so an SDV generator is run as a full arm of a study whose entire empirical program is generator behaviour.

No abstract or full text was available to describe the experimental setup or results. The paper cites the CTGAN (2019) paper, but how CTGAN is used -- as a generator run in the pipeline, a baseline, or only referenced -- cannot be determined from the metadata alone.

It targets civil-engineering material design, embedding physical constraints into the generative/predictive model to improve reliability under limited experimental data. TVAE, the variational-autoencoder synthesizer introduced alongside CTGAN, is modified with physics-informed constraints to form the paper's core predictive model.

paper-synner-synthetic-generator-framewo.summary: This paper introduces SYNNER, a synthetic data generation framework that uses knowledge graph embeddings to encode entities into a vector space and generate statistically consistent synthetic records, evaluated across seven public datasets for utility preservation and a novel differential-privacy adversarial-attack protocol. The authors compare SYNNER against synthpop, ARGN, and CTGAN across duplicate-rate and macro-F1 metrics on multiple datasets. CTGAN is run unmodified as one of several baseline synthetic data generators benchmarked against SYNNER.

paper-smartgen-synthesizing-context-awar.summary: This paper proposes SmartGen, an LLM-based framework that synthesizes context-aware user behavior data for smart homes, using time/semantic-aware sequence splitting, sequence compression, graph-guided synthesis, and outlier filtering to help downstream anomaly detection and behavior prediction models adapt to behavioral drift. It evaluates on three real-world smart home datasets, showing large improvements over static training. The original SDV paper is cited only in a list of prior works on sequence/network-data generation, with no SDV code run.

It appears to target settings with limited labeled tabular data, using image-based transformations as a substitute or complement to traditional tabular augmentation techniques. The evidence shows only a citation to the CTGAN paper, with no confirmed detail on how CTGAN is used in the experiments.

paper-tackling-imbalanced-chronic-obstru.summary: This paper builds a stacking-ensemble machine learning framework to predict 14-day readmission risk in COPD patients using real-world multi-hospital clinical data from Kaohsiung, Taiwan, addressing severe class imbalance in the minority (readmitted) class. The authors compare two independent minority-class oversampling strategies, CTGAN and kernel density estimation (KDE), across multiple augmentation ratios, feature configurations, and recall thresholds, finding KDE generally more stable but analyzing both extensively via MMD, entropy/information-gain, and ablation studies. CTGAN is run directly as one of the two synthetic data generators whose output feeds the entire downstream classification and evaluation pipeline.

paper-comparative-analysis-gans-adaptive.summary: This conference paper presents a systematic comparative evaluation of Generative Adversarial Networks and Adaptive Bayesian Networks (implemented via the R 'abn' package) for synthetic tabular data generation, testing across 12 benchmark datasets and 3 real-world domains (healthcare, finance, telecommunications) on statistical fidelity, privacy risk, computational efficiency, and downstream task performance. CTGAN is used as the representative GAN implementation for the GAN arm of the comparison, with the authors explicitly acknowledging use of the CTGAN software package. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional training are described as its key innovations and it is run as the GAN-side evaluation subject against the Bayesian network approach.

paper-multi-stage-framework-kawasaki-202.summary: This paper proposes a multi-stage AI framework for early detection of Kawasaki disease that combines clustering-based undersampling with synthetic data augmentation and a stacking ensemble classifier, trained on data from one Taiwanese hospital and externally validated on another. It compares three augmentation techniques—CTGAN, Kernel Density Estimation, and GAN-based Bayesian Logistic Regression—to expand the rare-disease minority class, reporting that CTGAN generalized best on the external validation set in some configurations while GANBLR won on others. CTGAN, run via the SDV Python library named directly in the software environment, is used as one of several synthetic data generators evaluated for minority-class augmentation, not modified or extended.

paper-synthesizing-electronic-health-rec.summary: This work synthesizes two electronic health record datasets—for diabetes risk forecasting and ICU outcome prediction—using a statistical model (Gaussian Copula Synthesizer) and a deep learning model (Conditional GAN Synthesizer) to protect patient privacy while preserving data utility. Synthetic data quality was evaluated with statistical and machine-learning efficacy metrics, and privacy was assessed via k-Anonymity, l-Diversity, and ε-Identifiability. Both SDV-named synthesizers, GaussianCopula and CTGAN, are run as the actual data generators underpinning the entire empirical pipeline.

paper-decision-framework-privacy-preserv.summary: This paper surveys existing generative models for synthetic tabular data and proposes a taxonomy of solutions organized by the privacy guarantees they offer, alongside a decision framework that uses privacy and utility metrics to help select a suitable privacy-preserving generative model for a given scenario. It is a survey/methodological framework rather than an empirical study with its own experiments, per the available abstract. The Synthetic Data Vault's foundational 2016 paper is cited as part of the background literature on synthetic data generation.

paper-membership-inference-attacks-feder.summary: This paper systematically studies Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) against federated learning models trained on a real-world healthcare dataset, introducing record-level and client-level MIA formulations and a threshold-tuning mechanism to strengthen attacks. It also examines whether synthetic data affects a model's resistance to MIAs, generating synthetic tabular datasets for both attack settings and validating them with TSTR accuracy and Wasserstein distance metrics. CTGAN is run directly as the synthetic data generator underlying the study's synthetic-data experiments, exploiting its conditional sampling design to produce record- and client-level synthetic datasets used throughout the empirical evaluation.

paper-empirical-impact-label-noise-2025.summary: This paper empirically investigates how label noise in the original training data affects synthetic tabular data generation, evaluating synthetic data quality, downstream machine-learning efficacy, and synthesizer training convergence across two noise-injection schemes and multiple noise levels. The entire experimental programme is built around three tabular synthesizers -- CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN -- run and compared side by side as the generators under study. CopulaGAN and TVAE, both part of the SDV family, are run as evaluation subjects alongside CTGAN throughout the empirical analysis.

paper-interpretable-deep-learning-framew.summary: This paper develops an interpretable deep learning framework to predict the shear strength of dry joints in ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) structures under conditions of limited experimental data. Given the title's focus on 'small sample regimes,' the work likely leverages data generation or augmentation techniques to compensate for scarce training data, though the mechanism is not confirmed by the available evidence. paper-analyzing-public-environmental-awa.summary: This study surveys 550 residents of Kayseri, Türkiye to identify demographic, behavioral, and attitudinal predictors of environmental awareness related to cycling, using bioinspired feature selection (genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization) and an ensemble of classifiers (notably CatBoost and LightGBM) evaluated via 10-fold cross-validation. To address underrepresented groups in the survey data, the authors apply a Generative Adversarial Network to synthesize additional records, improving class balance before classification. The GAN-based synthetic data generation step cites the CTGAN paper, but the abstract does not confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN implementation itself was run.

paper-creating-artificial-students-never.summary: This paper compares CTGAN against three large language models (GPT2, DistilGPT2, DialoGPT) for generating synthetic tabular student records to support learning analytics research while addressing data-privacy concerns. Using the Synthcity library's implementation, the authors run each generator on five real student datasets and evaluate the resulting synthetic data with statistical resemblance and ML-utility metrics, finding CTGAN competitive with, though not clearly superior to, the LLM-based approaches. CTGAN is run as one of four generative models compared throughout the empirical evaluation, invoked via the Synthcity library rather than the SDV package directly.

paper-crowd-counting-probe-requests-2025.summary: This paper proposes a privacy-conscious Wi-Fi probe-request crowd counting pipeline that uses random-forest feature selection on Information Elements and DBSCAN clustering for device counting, with a diffusion model used to generate synthetic tabular data to compensate for limited labeled data. The authors compare the diffusion model's synthetic output against a GAN-based approach via PCA of real, GAN-generated, and diffusion-generated data. CTGAN is cited as the origin of Conditional Tabular GAN for mixed-type tabular data generation, appearing only as a bibliographic reference framing the GAN comparison rather than as a run library.

The approach is further validated on two additional UCI datasets (Heart Disease, Breast Cancer Wisconsin). CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run as the core generative component producing the synthetic data that the entire CTGAN-RF empirical programme rests on.

paper-enhancing-local-explanations-gan-2.summary: This paper introduces FIRE360, a multi-faceted local explanation method for tabular data that produces feature importances, rules, counterfactuals, exemplars and counter-exemplars from a single pre-generated synthetic dataset rather than per-instance generation, improving efficiency and fidelity over prior XAI methods. The authors test CTGAN and TVAE as their synthesizers, explicitly using 'the implementation provided by the Synthetic Data Vault library (SDV)' and following SDV's hyperparameter tuning guidelines. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE are run directly as the synthetic-data generators underlying the whole explanation pipeline.

paper-ensembling-membership-inference-at.summary: This paper studies membership inference attacks (MIAs) against tabular generative models as a decision problem under uncertainty, running the largest synthetic-data privacy benchmark to date across 9 generator architectures, 57 datasets, and multiple MIA methods, and proposes unsupervised ensemble attacks that are more robust than any single attack. CTGAN and TVAE, from the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are included among the nine generative model architectures whose synthetic outputs are subjected to membership inference attacks in the benchmark.

The generator and discriminator of this reconstruction GAN are built by the authors following CTGAN's architecture, with tanh outputs for continuous values and Gumbel softmax for discrete values. It is evaluated on six tabular datasets of varying size, domain, and feature type, under privacy-conscious and class-imbalanced settings, comparing classification performance against baselines. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generators (alongside TabDDPM and CTGAN+) against which TabularMDLM's synthetic data quality is compared.

paper-generative-synthetic-banking-trans.summary: This paper proposes a synthetic banking transaction data generation framework using a hybrid Wasserstein loss combined with privacy leakage penalties and anomaly injection, aimed at balancing statistical fidelity with regulatory compliance (PCI DSS, GDPR, PSD2) for downstream fraud detection. It reports 94% downstream model performance retention on synthetic payment datasets while passing privacy and compliance audits. Both the SDV (Patki et al., 2016) and CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) papers appear only in the reference list, with no SDV-family term found anywhere else in the full text.

paper-improving-models-obesity-predictio.summary: This paper investigates whether synthetic data can improve machine learning models for early obesity prediction, using online survey data on social physical activity. The authors compare a plain GAN and a Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN), each generating 15,000 synthetic samples to augment the training set, and show both improve precision, accuracy, recall and F1-score while reducing class imbalance. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN architecture, is run as one of the two generative methods producing the synthetic minority/augmentation data central to the study's results.

The methods are evaluated on generation time, statistical similarity (using KSComplement and correlation similarity metrics) and downstream ML classifier performance, with CTGAN emerging as the best performer overall. CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN are run as evaluation subjects from the SDV single-table synthesizer family, and SDMetrics-style quality metrics are used to score their statistical fidelity.

CTGAN is run as one of several augmentation methods, with its generated minority-class samples evaluated via distribution overlap and t-SNE visualization, and the authors conclude it does not significantly outperform simple stratified sampling. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional design are described and its synthetic output is benchmarked against SMOTE, ADASYN, and a plain GAN.

It is evaluated on synthetic and real-world (biological and economic) datasets, comparing downstream utility metrics and correlation/divergence measures against standard WGAN and CTGAN. Experiments on Adult, Census, Credit, Covtype, and Intrusion datasets show AGBDT achieves better statistical similarity and machine learning utility than baseline models while offering a tunable privacy-utility tradeoff. CTGAN and TVAE (from the SDV family) are run as two of five baseline generative models across all statistical-similarity, ML-utility, and privacy-metric comparisons, evaluated but not extended or modified by the authors.

ISAP-GAN's synthetic datasets are compared for distributional fidelity and downstream utility against three baseline tabular GAN models, MedGAN, TGAN, and CTGAN, with results tabulated across multiple metrics. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline synthesizers for comparison, and its output is shown to be outperformed by the authors' proposed generator.

Using 12 cross-sectional medical datasets and 6354 variable-set variants, the authors generate synthetic data with 7 different generative models and assess how adding adjunct variables impacts evaluation metrics. CTGAN is used as one of the seven synthetic data generation models evaluated across this benchmarking programme.

To overcome the small, gap-ridden experimental dataset, the authors generate a 20,000-specimen synthetic dataset and show that XGBoost trained on it outperforms the experimental-only model, validating the synthetic data via K-S tests and correlation heatmaps. The Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) from the CTGAN paper is used as the generator producing the entire synthetic dataset that the improved predictive model is built on.

Experiments on Wikivoyage and Metro do Porto datasets show Bplug outperforms two existing open-source synthetic data packages, Synthia and SDV, at matching feature distributions and correlations, with much lower processing time. SDV's relational synthesizer, described as building a database model by intersecting related tables and computing their statistics, is run offline as one of two baseline generators against which Bplug is benchmarked.

paper-arf-detecting-ethereum-fraudulent-.summary: This paper proposes CT-ARF, an Ethereum fraud detection framework combining recursive feature elimination, a feature-weighting mechanism called ARFBoost, and a data-augmentation strategy called CTDA (Conditioned Table generative adversarial network-based Data Augmentation) to address class imbalance, evaluated with LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, AdaBoost, RF, DT, and KNN. The authors describe employing 'the CTGAN algorithm, as introduced by Xu et al.' (citing the 2018 TGAN arXiv paper) as the foundational generator for CTDA, training it with a TensorFlow backend and a custom hyperparameter table that does not match the sdv-dev CTGAN package's constructor arguments, suggesting an independent reimplementation rather than the library itself. CTGAN's conditional table-GAN design is adopted as the core mechanism for synthesizing minority-class fraudulent transaction data central to the paper's ablation-validated results.
paper-arf-detecting-ethereum-fraudulent-.needs: Unclear whether CTDA is a genuine reimplementation of CTGAN or a loosely related custom TensorFlow GAN; the hyperparameter table (max depth, max bin, RMSE loss) resembles boosting-model rather than CTGAN parameters, and the cited paper is actually TGAN (2018), not CTGAN (2019).

paper-does-differentially-private-synthe.summary: This study empirically evaluates whether statistical hypothesis tests (Mann-Whitney U, t-test, chi-squared, median test) run on differentially private synthetic data produce trustworthy Type I/II error rates, using DP histogram methods, MWEM, Private-PGM, and DP-GAN across real prostate cancer and cardiovascular datasets plus simulated data. To construct the simulated multivariate datasets used as ground-truth inputs before DP noise was applied, the authors used SDV's GaussianCopulaSynthesizer, trained on real-world data and conditioned to control the number of high-risk cases generated.

paper-enhancing-intrusion-detection-deep.summary: This conference paper proposes a deep neural network intrusion detection system for the highly imbalanced NSL-KDD dataset, using CTGAN-based oversampling to synthesize minority-class samples (Probe, U2R, R2L) before feeding a compressed feature representation into a DNN classifier, and reports large precision/recall/F1 gains over CGAN and WCGAN baselines. The authors cite the CTGAN paper for the architecture but state they implemented it via the third-party ydata-synthetic library (v1.3.1) rather than the sdv-dev package. CTGAN's conditional tabular GAN concept is the load-bearing generator for minority-class data synthesis, though the code executed was a separate library's implementation rather than SDV's own.
paper-enhancing-intrusion-detection-deep.needs: The CTGAN paper is cited as the source of the architecture, but the actual code run is the ydata-synthetic library, not the sdv-dev CTGAN package -- integration is judged as inherited rather than api_user on that basis.

paper-generating-manufacturing-distribut.summary: This paper proposes a deep-learning approach to reproduce realistic manufacturing variation distributions for sampling-based tolerance analysis, aiming to overcome the simplifying statistical assumptions of conventional sampling techniques and the cost of measuring novel manufacturing processes like additive manufacturing. It demonstrates the approach on illustrative tolerancing use cases with small real datasets. The work cites the TGAN paper (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) as related generative modeling work for tabular/synthetic data generation.
paper-generating-manufacturing-distribut.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was actually implemented/run for generating manufacturing distributions or merely cited as related work.

paper-impact-rain-frequency-bands-2024.summary: This paper studies how rainfall affects frequency band switching in 4G/5G mobile networks in outdoor industrial settings, using CNN classifiers trained on rainfall-related radio signal data to predict rain events. To address severe class imbalance in the training dataset, the authors generate synthetic samples for underrepresented classes, which raised classification accuracy from about 75% to 85%. CTGAN is run directly as the generator producing the synthetic minority-class samples used to augment the training data.
paper-impact-rain-frequency-bands-2024.needs: Evidence does not specify whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or another implementation was used, but the citation to Xu et al. 2019 and direct use as generator supports api_user classification.

paper-population-fidelity-estimator-util.summary: This paper investigates whether population fidelity metrics reliably estimate the utility of synthetic training data by correlating nine such metrics with the F1-performance of classification models trained on synthetic datasets. The authors generate synthetic data using CTGAN (and TVAE for one dataset) and compute several fidelity metrics via the SDMetrics library, finding only moderate and inconsistent correlations with downstream utility. CTGAN and TVAE are run as the generators producing the synthetic datasets under study, and SDMetrics is used directly to compute several of the population fidelity metrics evaluated.

paper-prediction-compressive-strength-fr.summary: This paper proposes a machine-learning framework for predicting the compressive strength of FRP-confined concrete, introducing a synthetic-data-driven approach presumably to expand limited experimental datasets for model training. No further methodological detail is available beyond the title and citation record. The work cites the TGAN (2018) paper from the SDV family, apparently as a source for synthetic tabular data generation.
paper-prediction-compressive-strength-fr.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether TGAN was implemented to generate synthetic training data or only cited as background, nor whether SDV's package or an independent reimplementation was used.

paper-prototype-oriented-hypergraph-repr.summary: This paper proposes a hypergraph-based representation learning framework that uses learned prototypes to detect anomalies in tabular datasets, aiming to better capture higher-order relationships between features and samples than pairwise graph methods. No full text was available, so the exact role of the cited work could not be verified. The paper cites the CTGAN paper from the SDV family, apparently in relation to tabular data modeling.
paper-prototype-oriented-hypergraph-repr.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is run as a baseline generator or only cited in related work discussion.

paper-qualitative-augmentation-performan.summary: This paper addresses data scarcity in VLSI circuit performance prediction by proposing a qualitative data augmentation approach, likely using generative modeling to expand training datasets for downstream predictive models. Its industry setting is VLSI circuit design and performance modeling rather than a generic benchmark study. It cites the TGAN paper as prior generative-modeling work relevant to synthesizing tabular circuit data for augmentation purposes.
paper-qualitative-augmentation-performan.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was run as a generator, adopted conceptually, or merely cited, so integration mechanism and true importance remain uncertain.

paper-tvae-ctgan-rigorous-2024.summary: Examines how CTGAN and TVAE behave as dataset scale varies, arguing that published comparisons rarely separate model quality from the size of the data each was fitted on. Both models under test are SDV's, so the paper is an experimental account of SDV's two deep synthesizers rather than a survey that happens to include them.

paper-synthetic-collision-prone-trajecto.summary: This conference paper proposes a pipeline for generating synthetic collision-prone vehicle trajectories to support testing and validation of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs), addressing the scarcity and privacy limitations of real-world crash data. The authors configure, condition, and train a CTGAN model on labeled real-world trajectory data (from ApolloScape and nuScenes) to produce diverse collision scenarios, comparing its output against TimeGAN and SocialGAN on realism, diversity, and coverage metrics. CTGAN is the sole generative model driving the entire empirical study, run to condition synthetic trajectory generation on collision-relevant labels.
paper-synthetic-collision-prone-trajecto.needs: Full text describes configuring generator/discriminator hyperparameters generically (learning rate, batch size) without naming the sdv-dev/ctgan package explicitly or listing its specific constructor parameters, so it is unclear whether the authors ran the official CTGAN package or built their own implementation.

paper-privacy-preserving-relational-synt.summary: This paper proposes a pipeline for generating synthetic multi-table relational data using probabilistic relational models, specifically parametric factor graphs, including a learning algorithm to construct such a model from a relational database. It positions this approach against existing single-table synthetic data generation methods based on GANs or Bayesian networks. CTGAN is cited only in the related-work discussion of GAN-based approaches, with no code run or comparison performed.
paper-privacy-preserving-relational-synt.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract-context sentence available, so deeper engagement with CTGAN (if any) cannot be verified.

paper-explainable-artificial-intelligenc.summary: This paper studies organisational agility and resilience ('regility') by building a machine-learning prediction model from survey data of 44 Australian industry participants and applying SHAP-based explainable AI to identify the features driving agility predictions. Because the collected survey sample was small, the authors used the Synthetic Data Vault Python package to generate additional synthetic data for the study, describing its four-step process (organise, specify structure, learn model, synthesise) drawn from the original SDV paper. SDV's relational/multi-table synthesizer (HMA-style modelling) is run directly as the tool that augments the limited empirical dataset underpinning the ML model.
paper-explainable-artificial-intelligenc.needs: The paper describes SDV's original multi-table API (database.get_table, synth_row, synth_children) verbatim from the 2016 paper rather than the modern sdv library API; unclear if a legacy or current SDV package version was actually run.

paper-survey-gan-techniques-augmentation.summary: This is a survey paper reviewing GAN-based data augmentation techniques proposed in prior literature for tackling class imbalance in credit card fraud detection, summarizing dozens of GAN variants (CTAB-GAN, SDG-GAN, cWGAN, etc.) and their reported strengths and limitations. It does not run any generator itself; it only recounts other researchers' experiments and comparisons. CTGAN is mentioned only as one of several baseline algorithms that a third-party study (Zhao et al.'s CTAB-GAN) compared against, and its cost-function mechanism is briefly described in prose.
paper-survey-gan-techniques-augmentation.needs: CTGAN is only described secondhand via another paper's comparison table; the survey itself never runs it.

paper-eeg-conditional-gan-augmentation-2.summary: Proposes a conditional-input temporal GAN for augmenting motor imagery EEG, combining adversarial training with a supervised autoregressive loss and an embedding and recovery autoencoder so that spatio-temporal structure survives generation, with class labels fed to both generator and discriminator through an extra input layer, and all four components built from three-layer GRU networks. Sample quality is assessed by an inverted Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic, KL divergence, SVC and logistic detection scores and a train-on-synthetic test-on-real predictive score, plus PCA and t-SNE views, and a 1D temporal CNN trained purely on synthetic EEG reaches 94.1 percent accuracy on real test data against 85 percent without augmentation. The paper is in the index because its entire comparison set is SDV: it benchmarks the proposed model against CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN and reports numbers for all three, and its discussion argues that CTGAN does not take the time factor into account, which is the gap the proposed architecture is built to close. CTGAN and TVAE are cited to Xu et al. 2019, and CopulaGAN ships only in SDV, so the trio identifies the SDV tabular API as the baseline suite even though the library itself is never named.

paper-automated-analysis-design-recycled.summary: This study develops a machine-learning framework (GA-XGBoost) for classifying failure modes and predicting capacity of recycled aggregate reinforced concrete (RAC) beams, trained on a compiled dataset of 276 tests, and builds a companion design framework plus a web app for practical use. For the design framework, a generative adversarial network for tabular data is used to generate synthetic data that provides candidate options for selecting design variables under specified constraints. The GAN for tabular data cited is TGAN (2018), used to produce the synthetic design-variable options underlying the design framework.
paper-automated-analysis-design-recycled.needs: No full text available; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev TGAN package was actually run or reimplemented, so integration is marked unclear.

paper-construction-two-stage-rockburst-2.summary: This paper builds a two-level machine-learning model for predicting rockburst risk in underground mining, first augmenting six rockburst features with distribution transforms and synthetic data generation, then reclustering labels with K-Means/ISOMAP before stacking eight classifiers and a deep forest for prediction. To address sample imbalance in the original rockburst case data, the authors generate synthetic rows to enrich the training set and compare the resulting Yeo-Johnson-CTGAN dataset against SMOTE oversampling, finding CTGAN's synthetic distribution closer to the real data by KL divergence. CTGAN (the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN) is run as the generator producing the augmented rockburst dataset that underlies most of the paper's downstream modeling and evaluation.
paper-construction-two-stage-rockburst-2.needs: No explicit package name, import statement, or constructor hyperparameters are given, so it is unclear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run directly or reimplemented from the original architecture description.

paper-centric-improve-churn-prediction-2.summary: This conference paper presents a data-centric AI benchmark for churn prediction, comparing seven data synthesis algorithms (SMOTE, SMOTENC, SMOTE-Tomek, Copula, Synthpop, CTGAN, TVAE) across three data strategies (substitution, balancing, augmentation) on four real-world churn datasets, evaluated with seven classifiers. CTGAN and TVAE are cited to the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper and run as two of the several generative models compared throughout the empirical study. CTGAN's conditional GAN and TVAE are run as evaluation subjects among the several synthesizers benchmarked for churn data resampling.
paper-centric-improve-churn-prediction-2.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev ctgan package or an independent implementation; no explicit package/API mention in the visible text.

paper-centric-improve-early-detection-20.summary: This paper argues for a data-centric AI approach to early mental illness detection, comparing eight established tabular data synthesis methods (SMOTE, ADASYN, SMOTETomek, Copula, Synthpop, CTGAN, CTAB-GAN+, TVAE) across data synthesis, balancing, and augmentation strategies, evaluated with six classifiers on a mental health survey dataset. TVAE was found to be the best-performing generative model overall, notably boosting Decision Tree performance. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian Copula are run as evaluation subjects among the eight generators compared, with TVAE emerging as the top performer.
paper-centric-improve-early-detection-20.needs: The 'Copula' method is presumed to be SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer given its co-listing with CTGAN/TVAE/CTAB-GAN+, but the text does not explicitly name the SDV library for it.

paper-adversarial-attacks-techniques-lea.summary: This paper is a survey of adversarial attack techniques (evasion, poisoning, inference), learning methods for understanding them via explainable AI, and defense/countermeasure strategies against AI-based systems, with emphasis on cybersecurity applications like intrusion and malware detection. It contributes a broad literature overview and a small anomaly/malware detection application to illustrate the discussed concepts. CTGAN is described in prose as a conditional GAN for tabular data with mode-specific normalization, cited for its use generating synthetic network traffic and adversarial malware samples, but is not run or implemented in this work.

paper-machine-learning-assist-auditory-2.summary: This clinical study applies Random Forest and XGBoost, interpreted with SHAP, to categorize children referred for auditory processing disorder (APD) assessment into clinical sub-groups matching expert audiologist labels, using retrospective data from 134 children. Because the dataset was small and imbalanced, the authors used CTGAN as a data augmentation technique to generate synthetic training samples, comparing it against SMOTE and reporting it significantly improved neural network accuracy. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling for imbalanced columns, is run as one of the augmentation methods evaluated in the study.

paper-automatic-self-calibrated-measurem.summary: This paper proposes a computer-vision pipeline that automates human body measurement from images or video using key-point detection, instance segmentation, and 3D model reconstruction, aiming to replace manual tailor measurements for the apparel industry. Facing insufficient training data, the authors briefly discuss data augmentation techniques and settled on Gretel.ai's synthetic data generator rather than the alternatives they mention. CTGAN is cited only in passing, alongside SMOTE, as one of the techniques researched but not adopted.
paper-automatic-self-calibrated-measurem.needs: No citing sentence or full text obtained; cannot determine why or how CTGAN is cited (likely unrelated related-work mention). Importance and integration are best guesses from a citation-only signal.

paper-cttgan-2022.summary: Addresses class imbalance in malicious-traffic identification by synthesizing minority-class samples, reporting recognition above 0.99 for MLP, KNN and SVM on the rebalanced set and improvement over oversampling and undersampling. CTTGAN takes CTGAN's conditional generator and its joint handling of discrete and continuous columns and retargets them at network traffic features; the entry records a derivative model, not a use of the library.

paper-anonymization-evaluation-big-iot-2.summary: This paper proposes a framework for evaluating data anonymization techniques in big data and IoT contexts, addressing how well anonymization methods balance privacy protection and data utility. It appears to survey or benchmark anonymization/synthetic-data approaches relevant to large-scale and IoT data pipelines. The original Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited, apparently as a reference point for synthetic data generation in the context of anonymization evaluation.
paper-anonymization-evaluation-big-iot-2.needs: Only metadata available (no abstract or citing sentences); cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed substantively or merely listed among anonymization/synthetic-data references.

paper-deep-entity-matching-adversarial-2.summary: This paper proposes DAEM, a deep entity matching approach that combines a deep neural model for record comparison with an adversarial active learning framework to reduce labeling cost and improve robustness on noisy textual data. It also introduces a dynamic blocking method for scaling to large databases, and evaluates on multiple benchmark entity matching datasets. CTGAN is run as a state-of-the-art tabular data generation baseline to augment training examples, and its performance is compared against the authors' adversarial learning approach, which consistently outperforms it.
paper-deep-entity-matching-adversarial-2.needs: Full text not available; unable to confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or a reimplementation, or details of how it was applied within the entity matching pipeline.

paper-explainable-machine-learning-real-.summary: The paper develops an ensemble of random forest, extreme gradient boosted trees, and deep learning models to predict fire resistance and fire-induced spalling of reinforced concrete columns, addressing the scarcity of fire test data by generating synthetic and augmented observations. It emphasizes explainability of the resulting 'black-box' predictions across a database of 494 real fire tests. Metadata indicates the paper cites the TGAN (2018) paper, but no passage referencing TGAN, SDV, or any related tool could be located in the retrieved full text.
paper-explainable-machine-learning-real-.needs: Full reference list not fully captured; cannot confirm how or whether TGAN is actually used or merely cited in the bibliography, since no matching passage was found in the extracted text.

paper-generative-models-age-race-2022.summary: This paper develops a custom GAN architecture to model a panel of physiological determinants of drug dosing (age, race/ethnicity, body weight, renal/liver biomarkers, etc.) derived from NHANES data, aiming to recapitulate real-world distributions and age/race/disease-state dependencies for pharmacometric applications. The authors build and evaluate their own GAN rather than using an existing library, comparing simulated and test data distributions. CTGAN's paper is cited only to justify a design consideration that tabular data lacks the local correlation structure found in images, with no CTGAN code or library run.
paper-generative-models-age-race-2022.needs: Confirmed no CTGAN code or library was run; citation is used only for a general design rationale about tabular data.

paper-reidentification-risk-estimator-20.summary: Develops a risk estimator for the sample-to-population attack, where an adversary picks a record from released microdata and tries to match it against the population, and validates it across health datasets. The estimator is copula-based: Gaussian and d-vine copula variants are compared, which places the vine copula line of SDV research inside a privacy-measurement method rather than a generator.

paper-mechanistic-modeling-explanatory-t.summary: This paper develops a Wilson-Cowan neural circuit model to relate medication dosages to changes in the Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale for schizophrenia patients with catatonia, aiming to explain treatment effect sizes and support individualized dosing decisions. To demonstrate the model's functioning without using the real clinical dataset directly, the authors synthesized surrogate data based on the statistics of their patient cohort's dosage and rating-scale records. They built this surrogate dataset using SDV's Gaussian copula synthesizer, run as the generator of the demonstration data.
paper-mechanistic-modeling-explanatory-t.needs: "SVD" appears to be a typo for SDV; interpreted as such given the citation to Patki et al. 2016 (The Synthetic Data Vault).

paper-privacy-utility-private-synthetic-.summary: This paper empirically evaluates three private synthetic data generators (MWEM, DP-CTGAN, and PATE-CTGAN) for a continuous heart-rate monitoring use case, measuring the privacy-utility trade-off across different differential-privacy epsilon settings. The generators tested are differentially private variants built on deep-learning architectures rather than SDV code itself; DP-CTGAN is described as using Xu et al.'s CTGAN model as its foundation. CTGAN is cited and its conditional-distribution mechanism for avoiding class imbalance is described in prose, but CTGAN itself is not run -- only its descendant DP-CTGAN is benchmarked.

paper-query-transformation-approximate-q.summary: This conference paper proposes query transformation rules for approximate query processing (AQP) engines that use synthetic data from arbitrary machine learning models, aiming to avoid dependence on any specific generative model. The authors run preliminary experiments generating synthetic versions of an Instacart grocery dataset and comparing AQP accuracy and execution time when the underlying synthetic data comes from different generators. CTGAN and TVAE, run via the open-source sdv-dev/CTGAN implementation, are the two synthesizers used to produce the synthetic data underlying the AQP evaluation.
paper-query-transformation-approximate-q.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the 'open source implementation' is the sdv-dev CTGAN package specifically, or verify how central the generated data is to the reported experiments beyond the abstract's mention.

paper-synthetic-subject-generation-coupl.summary: This work proposes methods to generate synthetic 'subjects' combining time series health data with subject metadata, addressing privacy concerns in health/well-being research where personal data protection limits research use of real data. Two approaches are proposed: one using real time series with synthetic metadata, the other generating both synthetically; the first is implemented and evaluated while the second needs further work. The SDV Python package is used directly, with its TVAE model (default parameters) run to generate synthetic subject data and its PAR model trialed for synthetic time series generation, though PAR's results did not meet similarity requirements.
paper-synthetic-subject-generation-coupl.needs: Full text not available; affiliations and exact venue could not be confirmed from abstract-level evidence.

paper-tabfairgan-fair-tabular-generation.summary: This paper proposes TabFairGAN, a two-phase GAN for generating tabular data that is both statistically accurate and fair with respect to a protected attribute, using a single critic and a fairness-constrained value function in its second training phase. The authors evaluate their model on several fairness-literature datasets and compare its accuracy and ML efficacy against other tabular GANs. TGAN and CTGAN are run as baseline generators in the experiments, with CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator described and its outputs directly compared in results tables against TabFairGAN.

paper-survey-synthetic-generation-machin.summary: A survey paper reviewing synthetic data generation methods with a focus on healthcare applications, summarizing prior studies on tabular, image, and medical data synthesis and their use for improving machine learning performance. It discusses a cited study (Dankar et al.) that compared four synthetic data generation techniques—Data Synthesizer, Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), and parametric/nonparametric Synthpop—for medical datasets such as breast cancer and dermatology. SDV is mentioned only as one of the techniques evaluated in that cited work, not run by the survey's own authors.
paper-survey-synthetic-generation-machin.needs: SDV is discussed only as part of a summarized third-party study (Dankar et al.), not run by the survey authors themselves.

paper-comment-gmd-2020-427-3-2021.summary: This is a peer-review comment on a manuscript that explores copula-based statistical models for augmenting training data for a machine-learning emulator of downwelling longwave radiation in a weather/climate context, reporting improved mean absolute error when copula-augmented synthetic data are used. The review comment itself is not available in full text, only its citation of the original SDV paper. SDV's foundational paper (Patki et al. 2016) is cited, but the evidence does not show how or in what context the review references it.
paper-comment-gmd-2020-427-3-2021.needs: Full text of the review comment (and the reviewed manuscript) is not available; cannot confirm whether SDV is engaged with methodologically or only cited in passing, nor what specific concept (e.g. Gaussian copula) is invoked.

paper-covid-severity-imaging-clinical-20.summary: Builds and validates models that flag severe or critical COVID-19 from routine clinical variables and CT-derived features across two Chinese hospitals, reporting AUC and F1 alongside SHAP attributions so clinicians can see which inputs drive a prediction. Severe cases are rare in the cohort, an imbalance ratio of 0.07, so the study tests four oversampling treatments to raise the minority share to 0.3 and measures the change each produces: SMOTE, adaptive synthetic sampling, geometric SMOTE, and CTGAN. For the CTGAN arm the model is fitted on the training set and sampled to top up the minority class, with results reported on the untouched test set, and oversampling is found to help F1 more than AUC. SDV's generator is thus run as one of four interchangeable treatments inside a study about clinical severity prediction.

paper-differentially-private-synthetic-m.summary: This paper proposes a differentially private synthetic data generation framework built on convolutional autoencoders and convolutional GANs trained with Rényi differential privacy, targeting medical record data and aiming to preserve feature correlations and temporal structure. It compares against several prior GAN-based tabular/medical synthesis approaches under a common privacy budget. CTGAN is cited only in related work, described as a model that handles mixed discrete/continuous tabular data but not run or benchmarked in the experiments.

paper-generating-plausible-counterfactua.summary: This paper proposes PIECE, a method for generating plausible counterfactual and semi-factual explanations for black-box CNN image classifiers by modifying 'exceptional' features to be 'normal' relative to the target class. It compares against other counterfactual explanation methods on image benchmarks, focusing on explanation plausibility rather than tabular data. CTGAN is only mentioned in passing as a future-work direction for extending the framework to tabular data.

paper-probability-elicitation-geostatist.summary: This paper proposes a geostatistics-based workflow to help geoscience experts elicit joint probability distributions (JPDs) of geological outcomes more objectively during hydrocarbon exploration, using stochastic reservoir realizations and pilot-point simulation. As a comparison method, the authors train CTGAN on their geostatistical dataset to generate large resampled datasets (10^6-10^7 samples) and build an alternative, smoothed version of the JPD, contrasting it against additive smoothing and the reference distribution. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run directly (crediting the freely available CTGAN Python code) as one of several alternative techniques for constructing the JPD.

paper-ttnet-tabular-transfer-network-202.summary: This paper proposes TTNet, a tabular transfer learning network that combines a Buc&Tab architecture imitating tree-based structures with a meta-transfer learning strategy to enable knowledge transfer from abundant source tabular data to scarce target data, showing improved accuracy and efficiency on benchmark and e-commerce datasets. The CTGAN paper is cited only in passing, apparently mis-attached to a claim about xgboost's tree-based performance on tabular data, with no synthetic data generation used anywhere in the work.
paper-ttnet-tabular-transfer-network-202.needs: The citation to CTGAN appears to be a mis-citation error attached to a sentence about xgboost; the paper has no genuine engagement with CTGAN or synthetic data generation.

paper-model-generate-dynamic-synthetic-2.summary: This PhD project position paper, conducted with the Norwegian Tax Department's National Registry as a case study, argues for machine-learning-based methods to generate synthetic test data that is dynamic, representative, and privacy-compliant for cross-organizational integration testing. It discusses related work including model-based legal-policy simulation and RNN-based text generation, without proposing or running an implemented system in this paper. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is discussed and critiqued in the related-work section as limited to stand-alone relational databases and lacking a mechanism for dynamic updates, but it is not run or extended in this work.
paper-model-generate-dynamic-synthetic-2.needs: Full text not obtained; only a fragment of the citing sentence is available, so the exact framing (critique vs. adoption) of the SDV reference cannot be confirmed.

paper-extending-inverse-frequent-itemset.summary: This paper extends inverse frequent itemset mining (IFM) with new constraint types (infrequency, duplicates) and structured schemas to generate synthetic datasets that reflect patterns of real data, analyzing complexity and accuracy for applications like NoSQL/social network data. It positions its own approach against other synthetic data generation methods discussed in related work. SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) is only cited and described in prose as a relational-database synthesis system, not run or compared experimentally.
paper-extending-inverse-frequent-itemset.needs: Full text not obtained; only the single citing sentence is available, so deeper engagement with SDV (if any) cannot be assessed.

preprint-joint-synthetic-housing-househo.summary: This paper presents a framework for constructing a joint housing-household inventory that links synthetic individuals and households to compatible housing units from the National Structure Inventory, combining synthetic population generation, a deep contrastive learning compatibility model, and hierarchical optimization-based allocation, evaluated on coastal North Carolina. The authors adopt TabDiff, a diffusion-based tabular generator, as their synthesis engine, and benchmark it against TVAE and CTGAN implemented via the SDV library, which perform markedly worse on fidelity, correlation, and mode-collapse metrics. SDV's TVAE and CTGAN are run as rejected comparison baselines against the paper's chosen generative model.

preprint-tdgt-tabular-generation-toolkit.summary: This paper introduces TDGT, a web-based toolkit for tabular synthetic data generation and fidelity assessment, centered on a novel Adaptive Bayesian Mixture Synthesizer (ABMS) and its VAE-hybrid and GPU-accelerated variants, alongside eleven statistical fidelity metrics and privacy risk indicators. It is evaluated across healthcare, socioeconomic, and cybersecurity datasets. In its related-work discussion of prior generative approaches, it cites SDV's CTGAN, CopulaGAN, TVAE and GaussianCopula as GAN-, VAE- and copula-based methods it positions its own ABMS/VAE-ABMS architecture against, without running them.
preprint-tdgt-tabular-generation-toolkit.needs: Full experimental section not shown in excerpt; unclear whether CTGAN/TVAE/GaussianCopula appear as baselines in later benchmarking tables beyond the related-work description given.

preprint-useful-private-synthetic-omics-.summary: A community benchmarking study from the CAMDA 2025 Health Privacy Challenge that systematically evaluates 11 generative methods for synthesizing bulk RNA-seq data across two cancer cohorts, measuring distributional fidelity, downstream utility, biological plausibility, and membership-inference privacy risk. CTGAN, along with a differentially private DP-CTGAN variant, is one of the generative methods benchmarked and is reported to suffer substantial loss of downstream predictive signal and near random-guessing membership inference risk. SDV's CTGAN model is run as one of several evaluation subjects rather than as the paper's own proposed generator.
preprint-useful-private-synthetic-omics-.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev/CTGAN package or reimplemented with a DP wrapper, so integration marked unclear.

preprint-generating-synthetic-formal-pri.summary: A survey mapping the landscape of privacy-preserving synthetic data generation across tabular, image, and text domains, covering theoretical foundations of generative models and differential privacy, and presenting an empirical study of four leading methods on five specialized real-world datasets to expose utility-privacy trade-offs under realistic privacy budgets. In its review of tabular generation methods, it cites CTGAN as one of several state-of-the-art models that rely on mode-specific normalisation via a variational Gaussian mixture model. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization technique is described in the related-work survey but not run as part of the paper's own experiments.
preprint-generating-synthetic-formal-pri.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN is one of the 'four leading methods' empirically evaluated on the five specialized datasets; no passage in the evidence shows it being run.

preprint-learning-represent-individual-d.summary: This paper investigates representation learning as a flexible method to capture individual differences in human choice decision-making, comparing embeddings from structured and unstructured data against traditional theory-based behavioral models. The authors show that representation-learning-based models improve prediction of economic decision-making choices over baselines lacking such representations. To address data scarcity at the 'cold start' of prediction, they use CTGAN to synthesize human choice data and run preliminary experiments mixing real and CTGAN-synthesized data to train prediction models.
preprint-learning-represent-individual-d.needs: Not explicit whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or a custom reimplementation was used; treated as api_user given no described custom architecture.

preprint-smote-improving-privacy-utility.summary: This paper proposes SMOTE-DP, a two-stage synthetic data generator pipeline in which a non-differentially-private generator (SMOTE) feeds a differentially private generator, aiming to improve the privacy-utility tradeoff over standard DP mechanisms. The authors prove theoretically and demonstrate empirically that this combination preserves downstream utility while maintaining strong privacy guarantees. CTGAN is cited only in passing, alongside other work, as an example of synthetic data techniques proposed to preserve statistical correlations while hiding personal information, without being run in the experiments.

preprint-unified-framework-tabular-gener.summary: This preprint proposes a unified framework for tabular deep generative modeling that adds a correlation- and distribution-aware regularization loss to existing generators, introduces a multi-objective Bayesian optimization strategy (IORBO) for hyperparameter search, and provides a benchmarking protocol across twenty datasets and ten baseline models. The framework is validated by modifying and retraining several generators, including CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN, with the new loss terms, alongside CTAB-GAN, DP-CGANS, and TabDDPM. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE architectures are directly extended with the authors' custom correlation/distribution loss and evaluated with and without conditional sampling, while CopulaGAN (Gaussian Copula + CTGAN) is run as one of the evaluated generators, making these SDV-family models a load-bearing part of the empirical programme.
preprint-unified-framework-tabular-gener.needs: Unclear whether the authors ran the actual sdv-dev/ctgan packages with modified loss hooks or fully reimplemented CTGAN/TVAE/CopulaGAN from scratch in PyTorch; hyperparameter names (embedding_dim, generator_dim, discriminator_dim, etc.) match the sdv-dev CTGAN constructor, suggesting library-based extension rather than pure reimplementation.

preprint-obfuscation-latent-space-projec.summary: This preprint proposes Latent Space Projection (LSP), a technique that uses autoencoders and adversarial training to obfuscate sensitive data in a lower-dimensional latent space while preserving utility for model training, validated on medical diagnosis and financial fraud case studies. The paper is an original privacy-preserving AI governance method rather than a synthetic-data benchmark or extension. CTGAN is only cited in passing as an example of GAN-based synthetic data generation in the related-work discussion, with no experiment run on it.

paper-harmonic-llm-synthesis-2024.summary: Fine-tunes a language model for tabular synthesis on an instruction set built by nearest-neighbour retrieval, so the model learns the relationships between a row's columns rather than memorising the rows themselves, and pairs it with a disclosure metric that scores how far generated records sit from their closest real counterpart. TVAE is one of the generators the result is measured against across machine-learning efficacy and likelihood metrics, and CTGAN is credited in the related work for introducing the conditional generator and for the machine-learning-efficacy benchmarking protocol the paper's evaluation is positioned against.

preprint-lost-averages-specific-setup-20.summary: This paper examines record-specific privacy games used to evaluate membership inference attacks (MIAs) against machine learning models and synthetic data generators, showing that the commonly used 'traditional' game averages a record's risk across datasets and can mislead when a specific model or dataset is released. The authors propose a 'model-seeded' privacy game, adapted from leave-one-out differential-privacy auditing, that yields a risk estimate specific to the actual released model or dataset, and validate it empirically across multiple datasets and models. CTGAN's original NeurIPS paper is cited only as a reference for prior tabular-data synthesis work, with no indication it was run as one of the evaluated generators.
preprint-lost-averages-specific-setup-20.needs: Full body text around the CTGAN citation was not surfaced beyond the reference list entry; unclear whether CTGAN was actually used as one of the evaluated synthetic data generators in experiments.

preprint-single-model-attribution-genera.summary: This paper proposes FLIPAD, a single-model attribution method that decides whether a sample was produced by a specific generative model, framed as anomaly detection over final-layer-inverted activations solvable as a convex lasso problem. The authors validate FLIPAD across image, tabular, and medical-image generators, including a tabular attribution experiment on wine-quality datasets. CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN were trained using the implementations and default settings provided by the SDV library as the tabular generators whose samples FLIPAD must attribute, alongside KL-WGAN.

preprint-synthetic-all-you-need-2023.summary: This preprint develops methods for performing membership inference attacks (MIAs) against synthetic tabular data without requiring the attacker to have an auxiliary dataset from the same distribution as the training data, proposing three attack scenarios of decreasing access (generator black-box access, synthetic dataset only, and a theoretical upper bound). It demonstrates that MIAs remain effective across two real-world datasets and two synthetic data generators. CTGAN is named only in the introduction as one example of a GAN-based synthetic data generator among a list of prior techniques, without being run or engaged with in detail in the evidence provided.
preprint-synthetic-all-you-need-2023.needs: Full text excerpt does not confirm whether CTGAN is one of the 'two synthetic data generators' used in the experiments; only an introductory citation is visible in the evidence provided.

preprint-frote-feedback-rule-driven-2022.summary: This paper introduces FROTE, a data augmentation method that oversamples synthetic instances guided by user-provided feedback rules to edit an ML model's decision boundary so it aligns with updated rules or regulations, evaluated on tabular datasets like loan approval and Adult. The method treats the downstream classifier as a black box and focuses on rule-driven relabeling and instance generation rather than generic generative modeling. The paper's metadata records a citation to the CTGAN paper, but no passage naming CTGAN, SDV, or any SDV-family component appears anywhere in the retrieved full text.
preprint-frote-feedback-rule-driven-2022.needs: Full text provided contains no SDV-family mention despite the citation record; cannot confirm how or whether CTGAN is discussed (likely a passing related-work citation on oversampling/GAN methods, but unverifiable from given evidence).

preprint-stan-synthetic-network-traffic-.summary: STAN proposes an autoregressive neural architecture combining CNN and mixture density network layers to synthesize network traffic data, capturing both temporal dependence and inter-attribute dependence for continuous and discrete variables, evaluated against simulated and real traffic datasets and downstream anomaly-detection tasks. In its related-work discussion the authors describe CTGAN as a GAN-based approach for generating general tabular data with mixed discrete/continuous attributes, contrasting it with Bayesian-network approaches, and cite vine copulas among traditional modeling algorithms limited by distributional assumptions. Both SDV-family methods (CTGAN and vine copulas) are discussed and critiqued as prior art rather than run in the experiments described.
preprint-stan-synthetic-network-traffic-.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN was actually run as one of the 'several baseline methods' mentioned in the abstract, which would raise integration to baseline_only and importance higher.

preprint-improving-missing-imputation-de.summary: This preprint surveys and compares deep generative approaches (VAEs and GANs) for imputing missing values in tabular data, proposing a backpropagation-based refinement technique and architectural adaptations for mixed categorical/numerical variables, tested on real-world datasets. In its related-work section it describes Tabular GAN (TGAN), noting its use of a recurrent neural network generator to output variable values in sequence for numerical and categorical data. TGAN is discussed only as prior art characterizing the field, not run in the authors' own imputation experiments.

preprint-survey-collection-machine-learn.summary: A survey of data collection techniques for machine learning, framed from a data management perspective and covering data acquisition, data labeling, and improvement of existing data or models across ML, NLP, vision, and database research communities. It catalogs prior work on synthetic data generation among many other data-acquisition techniques. The Synthetic Data Vault and TGAN are both cited only in the reference list as prior synthetic-data-generation work, with no body-text discussion or use of either.

repo-machine-learning-engineering-on-aws.summary: Companion code for a Packt title on machine-learning engineering with AWS services. Chapter one generates its working dataset with `CTGANSynthesizer`, so CTGAN is the source of the synthetic data every later chapter builds on rather than a topic the book covers.

repo-mlfrm.summary: Code accompanying an O'Reilly text on machine learning for financial risk management, one notebook per chapter. The synthetic-data chapter runs CTGAN and scores it with `sdv.evaluation`, with `ctgan` and `copulas` both pinned. SDV is the worked example a finance audience is taught on.
